frequency_question: How often do central banks implement targeted liquidity absorption ratios within a four-month horizon when short-term money market rates drop significantly below policy repo rates due to surplus liquidity?
membership_rule: Includes any emergency or discretionary reserve ratio requirement (such as incremental or ad-hoc cash reserve ratios) deployed specifically to mop up surplus liquidity; excludes routine annual policy rate changes or standard reserve requirement adjustments made during scheduled bi-monthly monetary policy reviews without an explicit liquidity-absorption mandate.
provenance_note: 2 cases named, 4 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (2.0x)
coverage_note: 2 explicit named instances of iCRR/incremental ratio deployment in past major surplus cycles out of 4 major liquidity overhang events; believed comprehensive for this specific instrument type.
known_gaps: Distinguishing between standard variable rate reverse repo auctions (VRRR) and statutory ratio changes (iCRR). iCRR is a rarer, heavier-handed tool used only during extreme liquidity overhangs.
skeleton: RBI liquidity management interventions over the past 20 years across distinct surplus liquidity cycles, multiplied by the frequency of deploying non-standard ratio hikes versus standard variable reverse repo operations.
multiplier: 2 targeted ratio implementations across 4 distinct liquidity overhang episodes in the past 20 years yields a base activation frequency of approximately 0.50 per major surplus cycle.
validity_reason: Central bank operational frameworks for liquidity management evolve slowly over multi-year structural regime changes.
